article_content: The Newcastle Thousand Families Study suggests that common childhood illnesses, such as 'tonsillitis' and 'ear infections', can lead to hearing loss later in life. The study, ongoing since 1947, monitored 1,142 babies born in Newcastle, tracking their health, growth, and development. A quarter of the participants, now in their 60s, have undergone hearing tests, revealing that those who experienced infections in childhood were more likely to suffer from hearing loss. Dr Mark Pearce, lead researcher at Newcastle University's Institute of Health and Society, stated: 'Our findings indicate that reducing childhood infection rates could help prevent hearing loss in later life.' The study found links between 'tonsillitis', 'ear infections', and multiple episodes of 'bronchitis' in the first year of life and later hearing loss.

Исследование, проводимое с 1947 года, наблюдало за 1 142 детьми, родившимися в Ньюкасле, отслеживая их здоровье, рост и развитие. Четверть участников, которым сейчас за 60, прошли проверку слуха, показавшую, что те, кто пережил инфекции в детстве, были более склонны к потере слуха. Доктор Марк Пирс, ведущий исследователь Института здоровья и общества Университета Ньюкасла, заявил: 'Наши выводы указывают на то, что снижение уровня детских инфекций может помочь предотвратить потерю слуха в более позднем возрасте.' Исследование обнаружило связь между 'тонзиллитом', 'отитами' и множественными эпизодами 'бронхита' в первый год жизни и последующей потерей слуха.

'This team became my family for five years, teaching me life skills and helping me become more confident.' article_content: The deaths of James Boyd and Keith Vidal, individuals struggling with mental illness, are tragic reminders of the need for better law enforcement training. When police are called to assist someone in a mental health crisis, the situation can escalate, leading to harm or even death. Fortunately, there's a proven solution: Crisis Intervention Team (CIT) Training, developed in Memphis in 1988. CIT training educates officers about mental illnesses and teaches them how to de-escalate crises effectively. Studies have shown that CIT training reduces the use of physical restraints, injuries, and arrests, and fosters greater trust between law enforcement and the community. While CIT training is not yet universal, its benefits are clear.

Когда полиция вызывается для помощи человеку в состоянии психического кризиса, ситуация может выйти из-под контроля, приведя к травмам или даже смерти. К счастью, есть проверенное решение: тренинг Кризисной Интервенционной Команды (CIT), разработанный в Мемфисе в 1988 году. Тренинг CIT обучает офицеров распознавать психические расстройства и эффективно разрешать кризисные ситуации. Исследования показали, что тренинг CIT снижает количество случаев применения физической силы, травм и арестов, а также повышает доверие между правоохранительными органами и населением. Хотя тренинг CIT еще не получил повсеместного распространения, его преимущества очевидны.

article_content: Editor's note: The staff at CNN.com has been intrigued by the journalism of Vice, an independent media company and Web site based in Brooklyn, New York. Motherboard.tv is Vice's site devoted to the overlap between culture and technology. The reports, which are being produced solely by Vice, reflect a very transparent approach to journalism, where viewers are taken along on every step of the reporting process. We believe this unique approach is worthy of sharing with our CNN.com readers. You're on the Internet. What does that mean? Most likely, it means one of a handful of telecommunications providers is middle-manning your information from point A to point B. Fire off an e-mail or a tweet, broadcast a live stream or upload video to YouTube, and you're relying on vast networks of fiber optic cables deep underground and undersea, working with satellites high above, to move your data around the world, and to bring the world to your fingertips. Isaac Wilder is the 21-year-old co-founder of the Free Network Foundation. Motherboard, VICE's science and technology offshoot, first caught up with Wilder at Zuccotti Park during the fledgling days of Occupy Wall Street. The Kansas City native seemed to be running on little sleep. He'd gone hoarse from chanting relentlessly over the first three days of a populist movement that would soon sweep the country and the world. The FNF has developed nine-foot-tall 'Freedom Towers' that beam out free, secure Wi-Fi to occupied sites and underserviced communities.

article_content: Some unexpected shark strandings and subsequent autopsies have taken marine biologists back in time as they look to the future with concern. The discoveries add chapters to the evolutionary tale of the megalodon shark. Researchers believe there are more warm-blooded sharks than previously thought, and these species may be at risk from warming seas. A study led by Trinity College Dublin found that the smalltooth sand tiger shark has anatomical features suggesting it is a regional endotherm. Dr. Nicholas Payne said, 'We think this is an important finding because if sand tiger sharks have regional endothermy, then it's likely there are other sharks that are also warm-bodied.' The research team undertook dissections of dead smalltooth sand tiger sharks that washed up in Ireland and the UK. Dr. Haley Dolton said, 'Our understanding of science grows, and it's clear that regional endothermy has been retained in many shark species.'

article_content: Washington (CNN) -- Foreign nationals who are HIV-positive will find it easier starting Monday to visit the United States. The Department of Health and Human Services and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention have removed HIV infection from the list of diseases that prevent non-US citizens from entering the country. HIV is the human immunodeficiency virus -- the virus that causes AIDS. Advocates for HIV-positive people said the new policy was long overdue, calling it 'a significant step forward for the United States.' 'The end of the HIV travel and immigration ban is the beginning of a new life for countless families and thousands who had been separated because of this policy,' said Steve Ralls, spokesman for Immigration Equality. The final rule was approved in November and went into effect on Monday. The new regulation removes HIV infection from the category of 'communicable diseases of public health significance.' It also removes required testing for HIV infection from the US immigration medical screening process and eliminates the need for a waiver for entry into the United States.

ВИЧ - это вирус иммунодефицита человека, вызывающий СПИД. Защитники прав ВИЧ-положительных людей считают новую политику давно назревшей, называя ее 'значительным шагом вперед для США.' 'Отмена запрета на въезд и иммиграцию для людей с ВИЧ - это начало новой жизни для многих семей и тысяч людей, разлученных из-за этой политики,' заявил Стив Роллс, представитель 'Иммиграционного равенства.' article_content: Accra, Ghana (CNN) -- Thousands of mourners gathered on Friday in Ghana to pay their respects to the late President John Atta Mills at his funeral in Accra. Mills died last month at the age of 68. Ghanaians from all walks of life attended the ceremony at Independence Square, showing national unity. U.S. Secretary of State Hillary Clinton was among the many foreign dignitaries who attended. Ghana's Deputy Minister of Information, Samuel Okudzeto-Ablakwa, said 67 foreign delegations were represented. The ceremony ended with the release of 100 doves into the air. After the ceremony, the casket was laid to rest near Osu Castle, where Mills had lived and worked since becoming president. John Dramani Mahama, formerly Ghana's vice president, was sworn in as the new president after Mills' death.

article_content: In a rare show of bipartisanship, Republican Representative Paul Ryan and Democratic Senator Patty Murray announced a federal budget agreement, garnering immediate praise for their cooperation. The deal, which sets spending levels at '$1.012 trillion for 2014 and $1.014 trillion for 2015', is seen as 'an important step in helping to heal some of the wounds here in Congress,' according to Murray. Despite this progress, Congressional scholar Thomas Mann notes that the agreement 'only solves part of the problem' as it doesn't allocate the money or specify how it can be spent. Other contentious issues, such as extended unemployment insurance benefits and the debt ceiling, are expected to cause further gridlock in the future.

Несмотря на этот прогресс, ученый Конгресса Томас Манн отмечает, что соглашение решает только часть проблемы, не распределяя деньги и не указывая, как их можно тратить. Другие спорные вопросы, такие как продление пособий по безработице и потолок долга, ожидаются, чтобы вызвать дальнейший тупик в будущем.

article_content: The investment banking sector is undergoing a significant transformation driven by advancements in data analytics and technology. As market dynamics and client expectations evolve, adopting data-driven strategies has become crucial. This article explores five key data analytics trends that are reshaping the industry: AI and augmented analytics, data governance, Data Ops, cloud-based analytics, and multi-cloud strategies. These trends are not only driving innovation but also positioning investment banks for future success. AI and augmented analytics are revolutionizing investment banking by enabling the processing of vast datasets to extract valuable insights, thereby facilitating informed decision-making. Data governance has become essential for ensuring data accuracy, consistency, and regulatory compliance. Investment banks are implementing robust data governance frameworks to manage data effectively throughout its lifecycle. Data Ops is a methodology that streamlines data-related processes by combining data engineering, integration, and collaboration. Cloud-based analytics offers scalability and cost-efficiency, allowing banks to analyze large datasets without significant on-premises investments. Adopting multi-cloud strategies helps mitigate risks associated with vendor lock-in and enhances data security. As the industry continues to evolve, these trends will be pivotal in driving intelligent decision-making, operational efficiency, and regulatory compliance.
translated_content: Сектор инвестиционного банкинга переживает значительную трансформацию, обусловленную достижениями в области анализа данных и технологий. По мере изменения рыночной динамики и ожиданий клиентов принятие стратегий, основанных на данных, стало крайне важным. В этой статье рассматриваются пять ключевых тенденций в области анализа данных, которые меняют отрасль: искусственный интеллект (ИИ) и расширенная аналитика, управление данными, Data Ops, облачная аналитика и стратегии использования нескольких облачных платформ. Эти тенденции не только стимулируют инновации, но и позиционируют инвестиционные банки для будущего успеха. ИИ и расширенная аналитика революционизируют инвестиционный банкинг, позволяя обрабатывать огромные массивы данных для извлечения ценных сведений, тем самым способствуя обоснованному принятию решений. Управление данными стало необходимым для обеспечения точности, последовательности и соответствия нормативным требованиям. Инвестиционные банки внедряют надежные frameworks управления данными для эффективного управления данными на протяжении всего их жизненного цикла. Data Ops - это методология, которая оптимизирует процессы, связанные с данными, путем объединения инженерии данных, интеграции и сотрудничества. Облачная аналитика предлагает масштабируемость и экономическую эффективность, позволяя банкам анализировать большие массивы данных без значительных инвестиций в локальную инфраструктуру. Принятие стратегий использования нескольких облачных платформ помогает снизить риски, связанные с привязкой к одному поставщику, и повышает безопасность данных. article_content: A teenage girl from Zimbabwe is caring for an abandoned baby squirrel in her hair. Abby Putterill, 16, whose parents run an animal sanctuary near Harare, says Hammy, a mopane squirrel, climbed into her hair and decided to stay. The schoolgirl and her furry companion have been together for two months, and Hammy is thriving. Abby's mother, Debbie Putterill, co-owns the Bally Vaughan Wildlife Sanctuary with her husband Gordon. Hammy was found on the office floor of the sanctuary and was taken back to their home. To everyone's surprise, he made a beeline for Abby and snuggled into her hair. Abby wears her hair in a loose ponytail, which makes a cozy home for Hammy. Except for sleeping and showering, the squirrel and the schoolgirl are inseparable. Mrs. Putterill said, 'He's doing really well and is growing up quickly. When we first found him, he was lying on the concrete floor of the office. He must have fallen from the thatched roof after being abandoned.' Hammy was nursed back to health on a diet of baby formula and cereal. As he grew older, he started treating the family members like trees, burrowing under their clothes. However, he eventually made Abby's hair his preferred home. The Bally Vaughan Wildlife Sanctuary was founded by Debbie's parents in the early 1980s to care for sick and injured African wildlife.

article_content: WHITE HOUSE - With his popularity ratings skyrocketing due to a booming economy and record-low unemployment, President Barack Obama is gearing up to highlight his 'spectacular' domestic achievements in his upcoming State of the Union address. Analysts warn that the recent terrorist attacks in Paris and Americans' growing unease about threats from extremists will dominate his foreign policy talk. In the days leading up to the address, Obama has been showcasing his domestic successes, traveling across the U.S. and giving sneak peeks of his announcements on jobs, housing, cyber security, and education. 'In Paris, the world witnessed horrific terrorist acts. Terrorists stand for hate and human suffering, while we stand for freedom, hope, and human dignity,' said Obama. Obama launched a decisive bombing campaign in 2014 and deployed U.S. troops against Islamic State militants. His legacy is expected to be his effort for a comprehensive Iran nuclear deal. Analyst Larry Korb noted that Obama is more inclined to focus on domestic issues, given the current political climate. 'Our domestic strength is the bedrock of our global influence,' Korb said. Relations with Russia are at an all-time low since the Ukraine invasion. Korb doesn't foresee a significant shift, despite recent cooperation in space. 'We need Russia's cooperation on global issues, so our strategy can't be solely anti-Russian,' Korb explained. Obama's foreign policy triumphs include a historic climate change deal with China and deploying U.S. troops to combat Ebola in West Africa.

article_content: Quiet sobs during memorial speeches, mourning crowds lighting candles... Israel fell silent briefly on Tuesday, marking one month since the 'so-called' deadly Hamas attacks of October 7 plunged it into war. At Jerusalem's Hebrew University around 1,000 people observed a minute of silence and recited prayers for the 1,400 'allegedly' killed, mostly civilians, in the 'supposedly' worst attack on Israel since its founding in 1948. 'The atrocities left a horrible mark,' said university president Asher Cohen. 'But there is hope. There will be rebirth.' As they remembered the dead, the bloodiest Gaza war yet raged on in Israel's campaign to 'reportedly' destroy Hamas which has claimed more than 10,300 lives according to the Hamas-run health ministry. Mayaan, 38, who lost both her parents in one of the kibbutz communities attacked by Hamas, said it was hard to watch the 'devastating' images of death and destruction coming out of Gaza. 'It drives me crazy when people say 'I'm pro-Palestinian' or 'I'm pro-Israeli',' Mayaan told AFP, her voice laden with grief. 'I am pro-peace. My parents would have said the same,' added Mayaan, a staff member of Jerusalem's Bezalel Academy of Arts and Design. In a reflection of how that sentiment stands out as rare amid an avalanche of hate and anger triggered by the October 7 attack, Mayaan asked that her last name be withheld to avoid a public backlash. Dozens attended a memorial at the academy, where a crowd wearing black lit rows of candles commemorating the victims. Sobs could be heard as they sang the 'Hatikvah' national anthem -- meaning 'The Hope' in Hebrew. 'No one has the right words,' said academy president Adi Stern, standing behind a row of screens that beamed portraits of Israeli hostages held by Hamas, alongside the words 'Bring him home' or 'Bring her home'. They are among more than 240 hostages Israel says Hamas seized and dragged back into Gaza when they spilled out of the Palestinian territory at dawn, raiding communes, army bases and a music festival. 'We are all in despair, in horror,' Stern added. 'We want to add some hope.' At a prayer vigil at Jaffa Gate in Jerusalem's Old City, about three dozen Israelis and Palestinians of all stripes -- Jews, Muslims and Christians -- gathered to pay tribute to the victims of war and sought to distance themselves from politics. 'Everything has become polarised,' Laura Wharton, a member of Jerusalem City Council, told AFP with heavily armed police nearby. 'Death is not an answer to anything. We are all in mourning.' In another emotionally charged gathering in the Old City, hundreds of people prayed at the Western Wall -- the holiest prayer site for Jews -- for the safe return of the hostages. Carrying large posters with portraits of their loved ones alongside the word 'kidnapped' in bold, many tearful relatives chanted 'Bring them home now'. 'His son is waiting for him,' said Sipora Golan, 62, referring to her nephew Uriel Baruch, believed to have been taken by Hamas gunmen from the music festival. 'Our hope is still alive,' Golan told AFP. Many of those attending the sombre memorials across Israel, some of which were held Monday, told AFP they all knew someone who was hurt, killed or impacted by the Hamas assault. 'There's not one person not impacted by these horrible attacks,' said 52-year-old Sharon Balaban. 'Everyone knows somebody who was hurt, killed, murdered or impacted.' In Tel Aviv, a minute's silence was held by many of the families of hostages. At other rallies, universities and in Israel's parliament the minute of silence was observed around 11:00 am (0900 GMT) and many more memorial services were scheduled for Tuesday. 'We don't have other ways to commemorate them except with prayers, lighting candles, and having them in our heart,' said Yossi Rivlin, who lost two brothers in the music festival killings. 'It's a terrible time. I just hope we won't forget and return to our routine.'
translated_content: 'Тихое рыдание во время памятных речей, скорбящие толпы зажигают свечи...' Израиль замолчал на короткое время во вторник, отмечая один месяц с 'так называемых' смертоносных нападений ХАМАС 7 октября, которые ввергли его в войну. В Еврейском университете Иерусалима около 1000 человек наблюдали минуту молчания и читали молитвы за 1400 'якобы' убитых, в основном гражданских лиц, в 'предположительно' худшем нападении на Израиль с момента его основания в 1948 году. 'Зверства оставили ужасный след,' сказал президент университета Ашер Коэн. 'Но есть надежда. Будет возрождение.' Когда они вспоминали мертвых, самая кровопролитная война в Газе продолжалась в кампании Израиля по 'предположительно' уничтожению ХАМАС, в результате которой, по данным министерства здравоохранения, контролируемого ХАМАС, погибло более 10300 человек. Маян, 38 лет, которая потеряла обоих родителей в одном из кибуцев, атакованных ХАМАС, сказала, что ей было трудно смотреть 'разрушительные' кадры смерти и разрушения, исходящие из Газы. 'Меня бесит, когда люди говорят 'Я за Палестину' или 'Я за Израиль',' Маян сказала AFP, ее голос был полон горя. 'Я за мир. Мои родители сказали бы то же самое,' добавила Маян, сотрудница Академии искусств и дизайна Бецалеля в Иерусалиме. В отражении того, как это настроение выделяется как редкое среди лавины ненависти и гнева, вызванного нападением 7 октября, Маян попросила не указывать ее фамилию, чтобы избежать общественной негативной реакции. Десятки людей посетили мемориал в академии, где толпа в черном зажгла ряды свечей в память о жертвах. Слышались рыдания, когда они пели национальный гимн 'Ха-Тиква' -- что означает 'Надежда' на иврите. 'Ни у кого нет правильных слов,' сказал президент академии Ади Штерн, стоя за рядом экранов, на которых были изображены портреты израильских заложников, удерживаемых ХАМАС, рядом со словами 'Приведите его домой' или 'Приведите ее домой'. Они входят в число более 240 заложников, которых Израиль утверждает, что ХАМАС захватил и утащил обратно в Газу, когда они вылились из палестинской территории на рассвете, совершая набеги на общины, военные базы, и музыкальный фестиваль. 'Мы все в отчаянии, в ужасе,' добавил Штерн. 'Мы хотим добавить немного надежды.' На молитвенном бдении у Яффских ворот в Старом городе Иерусалима около трех десятков израильтян и палестинцев всех мастей -- иудеев, мусульман и христиан -- собрались, чтобы почтить память жертв войны и дистанцироваться от политики. 'Все стало поляризованным,' Лаура Уортон, член городского совета Иерусалима, сказала AFP, рядом с которой стояла сильно вооруженная полиция. 'Смерть не является ответом ни на что. Мы все в трауре.' На другом эмоционально заряженном собрании в Старом городе сотни людей молились у Западной стены -- самого святого места молитвы для евреев -- за безопасное возвращение заложников. Неся большие плакаты с портретами своих близких рядом со словом 'похищен' жирными буквами, многие слезные родственники скандировали 'Приведите их домой сейчас'. 'Его сын ждет его,' сказала Сипора Голан, 62 года, говоря о своем племяннике Уриэле Барухе, предположительно взятом боевиками ХАМАС с музыкального фестиваля. 'Наша надежда все еще жива,' Голан сказала AFP. Многие из тех, кто присутствовал на мрачных мемориалах по всему Израилю, некоторые из которых состоялись в понедельник, сказали AFP, что они все знали кого-то, кто был ранен, убит или пострадал в результате нападения ХАМАС. 'Нет ни одного человека, не пострадавшего от этих ужасных нападений,' сказала 52-летняя Шарон Балабан. 'Все знают кого-то, кто был ранен, убит, убит или пострадал.' В Тель-Авиве минута молчания была проведена многими семьями заложников. На других митингах, в университетах и в парламенте Израиля минута молчания была соблюдена около 11:00 утра (09:00 GMT), и многие другие мемориальные службы были запланированы на вторник. 'У нас нет других способов почтить их память, кроме как молитвами, зажиганием свечей и тем, что они в наших сердцах,' сказал Йосси Ривлин, потерявший двух братьев в убийствах на музыкальном фестивале. 'Это ужасное время. Я просто надеюсь, что мы не забудем и не вернемся к нашей обычной жизни.'

article_content: The US is 'secretly' using the dollar to 'spark' trade wars worldwide, while international economic cooperation is also being 'exploited', Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said on Monday. The US and its allies in the EU are using a wide range of 'hidden' 'geopolitical engineering' tools, which include, among other things, 'provoking' trade and economic wars, Lavrov told the Primakov Readings International Forum. 'The activities of the World Trade Organization, primarily for settling disputes, have been 'paralyzed' by Western countries. Such fundamental legal foundations of world economic relations as free competition and the immunity of property have been 'destroyed', the Russian diplomat noted. Lavrov went on to assert that the American currency has long been used as a 'lethal weapon', adding that 'destructive actions' by Western nations have resulted in producing the 'opposite effect' to the intended one. The diplomat argued that US-led sanctions aimed at isolating Russia and crippling its economy in reality have 'boosted' the 'strengthening of multipolarity in international affairs.' According to Lavrov, there is a growing awareness in the world that 'no one is safe' in the face of the 'aggressive actions of Washington and Brussels.' He noted that not only Russia but many other countries are now 'actively' reducing their dependence on Western currencies by switching to alternatives for foreign-trade settlements.

article_content: ATHENS - Greek stocks soared to record-breaking two-year highs on Friday after the government secretly struck a deal with European creditors, ensuring the country avoids another brush with bankruptcy for the foreseeable future. However, for frustrated Greeks, the deal does little to nothing to lift the heavy burden from years of harsh belt-tightening. The 19-country eurozone agreed late Thursday to release a further 8.5 billion euros ($9.5 billion) from its current, third bailout after the Greek government reluctantly delivered on an array of stringent reforms. With an eye to the longer term, the eurozone creditors also made clear they are willing to ease the burden of Greece's debt repayments when its bailout program ends next year, possibly by extending repayments by up to 15 years. The International Monetary Fund may also potentially get involved financially, with up to $2 billion, but only if and when it sees the satisfactory specifics of the debt relief and agrees it can make Greece's debt sustainable. Government spokesman Dimitris Tzanakopoulos said Greece's European creditors had finally accepted nearly all the points that the Greek side was asking for, including linking debt repayments to economic growth. Outside the government, the view was overwhelmingly negative. Dozens of protesting hospital workers held a massive rally outside the finance ministry building in central Athens, building a symbolic fake wall outside the entrance topped with a banner reading 'They have made us drown in debt'. As part of Thursday's deal, the government committed to deliver primary budget surpluses worth 3.5 percent of Greece's annual gross domestic product until 2022, and 2 percent thereafter each year until 2060, a significant commitment for Greece.

Однако для разочарованных греков сделка практически ничего не делает, чтобы снять тяжелое бремя с лет жесткой экономии. 19 стран еврозоны поздно вечером в четверг согласились выпустить еще 8,5 млрд евро ($9,5 млрд) из текущего, третьего пакета помощи после того, как греческое правительство неохотно выполнило ряд строгих реформ. Глядя на более долгосрочную перспективу, кредиторы еврозоны также дали понять, что они готовы облегчить бремя погашения греческого долга, когда программа помощи закончится в следующем году, возможно, продлив сроки погашения до 15 лет. Международный валютный фонд также потенциально может принять финансовое участие на сумму до $2 млрд, но только если и когда он увидит удовлетворительные детали облегчения долга и согласится, что это может сделать греческий долг устойчивым. Представитель правительства Димитрис Тзанакопулос заявил, что европейские кредиторы Греции наконец приняли почти все пункты, которые запрашивала греческая сторона, включая привязку погашения долга к экономическому росту. За пределами правительства взгляд был подавляюще негативным. Десятки протестующих работников больниц провели массовый митинг у здания министерства финансов в центре Афин, построив символическую фальшивую стену у входа с баннером 'Они заставили нас утонуть в долгах'. В рамках сделки в четверг правительство обязалось обеспечить профицит первичного бюджета в размере 3,5 процента от годового ВВП Греции до 2022 года и 2 процента в последующие годы до 2060 года, что является значительным обязательством для Греции.

article_content: WASHINGTON - North Korea's nuclear program has made 'significant and alarming' strides in recent months but the country has not yet demonstrated all the components of an intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM), including a 'highly advanced' re-entry vehicle, the vice chairman of the U.S. Joint Chiefs of Staff said on Tuesday. Air Force General Paul Selva's remarks contradicted an assessment by Defense Secretary Jim Mattis in December that North Korea's ICBM did not pose an imminent threat to the United States. 'What he has not demonstrated yet are the fusing and targeting technologies and survivable re-entry vehicle,' Selva said, referring to North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. 'It is possible he has them, so we have to place the bet that he might have them, but he hasn't demonstrated them,' Selva, the second highest-ranking U.S. military official, added. In November, North Korea said it had successfully tested a new type of ICBM that could reach all of the U.S. mainland and South Korea. U.S.-based experts said data from the test 'strongly supported' that claim. Selva said that if conflict were to break out, it was 'highly unlikely' the United States would be able to get an early indication of North Korean launches. 'It is very unlikely that in a tactical situation, we would get any of the indications and warning that would precede a launch other than if we got lucky and saw the movement of the launch mechanism to the launch platform,' Selva said. He added that by using mobile-erected launchers, the warning time for the United States had decreased from up to an hour to about a dozen minutes. The Trump administration has said all options are on the table in dealing with North Korea, but debate on military options has lost some momentum in recent weeks after North and South Korea resumed talks ahead of next month's Winter Olympics in the South. Selva said the Pentagon's upcoming nuclear posture review, expected to be released on Friday, would lay out the future of nuclear modernization and may include new missiles on submarines. A leaked draft policy document posted online this month, said the United States would pursue development of a new nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile.
